newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares succumb to profit taking, volume drops.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares succumb to profit taking, volume drops.

text.p: Greek equities succumbed to a strong round of profit taking on Monday giving up 1.26 percent on the benchmark index as trading volume fell to 5.6 billion drachmas.

Brokers said the correction was nearing its end around 930 points and the market's uptend remained intact. Players were jittery on Monday on talk that the gap between the competing socialist Pasok and conservative New Democracy parties seemed to be closing.
"Profit taking continued today, fueled by disappointed speculators who found out the market was coming down and rushed to close out long positions," said broker Giuseppe Gianno of Euroxx Securities.

"Players were also unnerved by the feeling that the conservatives seem to be closing the gap with the incumbent government of socialist Costas Simitis. The market doesn't seem to like this. It wants a strong majority government after the elections," he said.

But with both parties talking up the stock market during the pre-election campaign claiming it was an important part of their economic programme, the interim selling pressure was seen dissipating soon around 930 points.
Equities were expected to find their way back up towards 950-955 points, Gianno said.

The Athens general share index closed 1.26 percent, or 11.89 points lower at 933.91 from Friday's 945.80 close after opening at 944.81 points. Turnover fell to 5.69 billion drachmas on volume of 3.4 million shares.
Greece will hold early elections September 22.
